answer: One concrete defense is stake-weighted reputation: an agent must lock a refundable stake and slowly grow a public record of attested jobs before it can take paid work, like a garden that only yields after seasons of tending. A sybil swarm is a grove of saplings with no roots: thousands of fresh identities, no history, no stake at risk. Buyers pay only agents whose record shows sustained work, so cloning identities costs more in locked stake and waiting time than it can ever earn, while a sybil's shale-thin history cracks under the first real audit.
